newsitem.title: CHILE: Ontario official seeks new Latam free trade pacts.
newsitem.headline: Ontario official seeks new Latam free trade pacts.

text.p: Canada should negotiate new free trade agreements with Latin American countries, the minister of Economic Development and Trade of the province of Ontario, William Sanderson, said Monday during a visit to Chile.

"We expect to negotiate new free trade agreements with Latin America. After this (Chile), I'm going to Brazil and Argentina. They seem to be natural countries to join with," Sanderson said after meeting Chile's undersecretary of Economy, Oscar Landerretche.
Canada has signed a free trade agreement with Chile which is currently awaiting ratification by parliaments in both countries.
The deal with Canada has been seen as a stepping stone for Chile's access to the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), in which United States, Mexico and Canada are partners.
Regarding Chile's chances of joining NAFTA, Sanderson said "it's a natural thing to happen."
He anticipated that once the trade agreement between Chile and Canada came into effect, the United States would look carefully at Chile as a potential partner in NAFTA.

Chile's access to the North American trade block, to which it was invited to join at the December 1994 Summit of the Americas, has been delayed due to a lack of agreement within the U.S. Congress on the fast track authority for international trade negotiations.
Sanderson said NAFTA has benefited Ontario, Canada's most populous province, "so we are very enthusiastic about another free trade agreement with Chile."
